small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_M tiles (e.g. 128/256 with BLOCK_N=64) to the gemm_logsumexp autotune list — M=16384 is huge so amortizing K-loop overhead with bigger row tiles should help; also try BLOCK_K=128 configs since K=4096 is large and contiguous.
- For gemm_sigmoid_kernel, since K=2048 and N=4096, drop the mask_k check on the inner K-loop when K % BLOCK_K == 0 (use a compile-time EVEN_K constexpr) to remove a per-iter mask and improve pipelining; same for gemm_logsumexp.
- Try num_stages=4-5 with BLOCK_K=64 on gemm_sigmoid for better K-loop overlap on RTX 4090, and add a (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=4, stages=5) candidate.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the entire pipeline into a single persistent kernel: each program owns a row-tile of M, streams the hidden activation through registers/SRAM tile-by-tile (compute sigmoid(x@W1+b1) for a BLOCK_H slice, immediately use it as the left operand of a second tl.dot against a BLOCK_H × BLOCK_N slice of W2, accumulate into the per-row online LSE state). This eliminates the 16384×4096 hidden write/read (~256 MB roundtrip) which currently dominates bandwidth.
- Alternatively, split-K the second GEMM with atomic combine of (max, sum) pairs — but the fused-pipeline approach is preferable since the hidden tensor materialization is the main waste.
- Consider FP16/BF16 tensor-core path for the GEMMs (cast inputs to bf16 on load, keep fp32 accumulator) to roughly double tensor-core throughput on the 4090, since tolerance is 5e-2.
